text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it as cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: you move things around to make them easier to find, but you don’t throw away any valuable items. The main goal is to make the code more readable and easier to maintain. For example, you might break a long, complicated function into smaller, clearer ones, or rename variables so their purpose is obvious. This practice helps reduce "technical debt"—the hidden cost of messy code that slows down future work. By refactoring regularly, you keep your project healthy, saving time and frustration in the long run.
